summary: I built R2-m6's decided smallest fix. C-007 now turns CRLF into LF in the harness output before it checks that each import-rule name is there, so a name whose yaml leaves a newline in it still matches: `name: >` ends in one, and a multi-line `name: |` holds one and ends in one. The harness prints that newline as CRLF on Windows; Get-ImportRuleNames returns LF. Shape-ImportRuleNames now feeds both spellings. It passes under both hosts with 11 import rules named, and without the normalisation it fails on exactly those two probes. This is the fifth finding in a row against the same text comparison (R2-m2, m3, R2-m4, m5, R2-m6). Each fix closes one axis on which two independently written spellings disagree, and the next axis can always be named. The structural fix is still unbuilt and is in follow_ups for a person to rank.

files.why: O-029: C-007 checks each import-rule name against the harness output after turning CRLF into LF. A comment explains why.

O-029: Shape-ImportRuleNames adds two probes. `name: >` (clip chomping) gives a name ending in a newline; `name: |` across two lines gives one that holds a newline and ends in one. The comment listing the spellings fed is updated, so the shape's title now matches what it feeds.

obligations.how: Built the decided smallest fix. In C-007, `$output = $run.Output.Replace("`r`n", "`n")` comes before the `Contains("'$_'")` check. Shape-ImportRuleNames feeds a `name: >` probe and a two-line `name: |` probe. The shape exits 0 in 101 s: the copy AGREEs at 11/15/27/60, and C-007 exits 0 under powershell.exe and pwsh with 'the 11 import rule(s) are named NOT RUN … (unnamed: )'. With the normalisation removed (bytes restored afterwards and SHA-256 checked), it exits 1 with 'unnamed: the provider's clipped folded probe never imports Core⏎, the provider's literal probe⏎…'. The harness line shows those names printed with CRLF inside the quotes.

follow_ups: Loop, now five laps: R2-m2 (quoting), m3 (wrapping), R2-m4 (yaml syntax), m5 (console escaping) and R2-m6 (line endings) are all the same comparison. C-007 re-derives each import-rule name and searches for it as quoted text in the harness's human-readable NOT RUN line. Every fix was right and every one closed only the axis named. Other axes are still open, for example a name containing `', '` or a single quote next to the list separator. The one change that closes the class is for the harness to also print a machine-readable line, e.g. `harness: not-run-json <json.dumps(names)>` (ASCII by default, no newlines), and for C-007 to parse that list and compare it with Get-ImportRuleNames' raw yaml.safe_load names, with no say()-spelling step. That changes harness.py's output contract, which is why this attempt built only the smallest fix R2-m6's decision chose. It is for a person to rank, rather than a sixth reviewer filing the next axis.
not_built: The structural fix R2-m6 also offered, a machine-readable `harness: not-run-json` line compared as a list. R2-m6's decision directed the smallest fix (CRLF normalisation plus the `>` and `|` probes), and the structural one is recorded in follow_ups.
